candidates.text:
Head of Content is becoming the most in-demand hire in tech right now.

I’m on 20+ calls a week with founders and their marketing leads, and the reason comes up on almost every one.

Building got cheap, a small team is now shipping so many new products and features.

A founder put it to me pretty plainly last week: "The tech isn’t the hard part anymore, anyone can copy it. The hard part is getting people to use it."

At the same time, buying attention keeps getting more expensive.

Ads costs are rising. Influencer marketing, especially in tech niches, are through the roof. 

So companies are doing the math. They can either pay an influencer 5k for one creator sponsored video on YouTube, or they can hire a fulltime person to lead all their content efforts on social media.

These companies are realizing the importance of building a channel they own, and they need someone who can take full ownership of this growing priority.

candidates.text:
if you’re a young designer who’s seeing this and thinking “so this is what it takes to get a design job today? this is what I’m up against?” you’re completely missing the point.

what stands out here isn’t the effort (which is considerable, yes), it’s the individuality. the creativity. the bravery. the delightful, memorable surprise of it all. most designers would never do something like this but the fact that Darshita has tells us something about who she is and what she’s capable of. she’s earned our attention simply by being so thoroughly herself, and I’d be shocked if she doesn’t have multiple competing offers in hand very soon.

herculean effort and 11/10 execution aren’t the only ways to get attention. sometimes the lowest-effort content is the most viral. but the stuff that breaks through and resonates widely always, always, always reflects an authentically unique point of view. a singular identity. if you take nothing else away from Darshita’s example, let it be that.

if you tell yourself a story that doing something this memorable is impossible for you, you will almost certainly be right. but it won’t be for lack of resources and support, it will be for lack of courage and self-knowledge. in the immortal words of Stephen Sondheim, “anything you do, let it come from you, then it will be new. give us more to see.”

candidates.text:
I rarely call out brands publicly, but this one genuinely hurts.

I’ve followed @GullyLabs since its inception, worn two pairs of their sneakers at my wedding, and recommended them to countless friends. I’ve always rooted for what @arjuns__ , Animesh and the team are building!

But this Durga Puja, they’ve lost me as a customer.

I ordered their special-edition Puja sneakers on October 12, specifically to wear during the festival. The website promised dispatch in 2 days. Eight days later, Puja is almost over, the shoes haven’t shipped, and there’s still no clear update.

What made it worse was the store experience.

After being told the pair was available in Bengaluru, I went to the store, only to be told otherwise. The salesperson then tried to pass off last year’s edition as the current one, couldn’t explain the differences, and was outright rude and dismissive when questioned.

For a sneaker brand built around culture, storytelling, and community, you’d expect the people representing it to understand both the product and the customer.

I’ve seen @arjuns__ & @GullyLabs talk so much about putting culture and customers at the heart of what they do. But culture isn’t just about the stories you tell or the sneakers you sell. It’s also about how you treat the people who believe in your brand.

I wasn’t just buying another pair of sneakers. I was buying something special for a festival that means a lot to me and my wife.

And that experience is now gone.

It’s disappointing to see a brand I’ve genuinely cherished since day one get something so fundamental so wrong.

You’ve lost a loyal customer, Gully Labs. And that genuinely makes me sad.

If something comes up, you just text him. He moves it and lets the other person know.
